# Leaf

> Leaf is a free, open-source ebook reader for macOS that opens a book like a document: double-click an EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, PDF, FB2 or CBZ file in Finder and it opens in its own window; close the window and the app quits. It has no library, no import, no account and makes no copies; it keeps only your reading position, highlights, notes and bookmarks, stored in its own folder and matched to the book by file content, never written into the book file. While you read, it shows time left estimated from your own reading speed, location numbers, typography presets, footnotes in place and find in book; you can highlight in four colors, add notes, bookmark pages, look up words in one step and export everything as Markdown or in Kindle’s My Clippings format. Native SwiftUI app, about 5 MB, macOS 15 or later. GPL-3.0 License. Independent project, not affiliated with Amazon.

Leaf is built with SwiftUI and WebKit and uses foliate-js to parse and paginate books. It deliberately has no bookshelf, library, store or sync: you double-click a file, read, and close the window. MOBI and AZW3 files must be DRM-free; books bought from the Kindle Store usually carry DRM and cannot be opened.

## Key facts

- Formats: EPUB, MOBI, AZW3 (DRM-free), PDF, FB2 and FBZ, CBZ comics
- PDF: shown as its original pages (PDFKit) with contents from the PDF outline, find, zoom, themes and go to page; typography settings do not apply
- Platform: macOS 15 or later; universal app for Apple silicon and Intel Macs
- Price: free; source code under the GPL-3.0
- Download: about 5 MB DMG
- Reading position: remembered per book, identified by file content (survives renaming or moving)
- Progress: click the bottom-right corner to cycle percent, location, time left in chapter, time left in book; estimates learn from your own page turns
- Contents: floating panel (⌘T or click the chapter name), highlights the current chapter, closes on selection
- Find in book: ⌘F, results listed by chapter with matches highlighted on the page; ⌘L jumps to a percent or location
- Highlights and notes: select text to highlight (yellow, green, blue, pink) and attach a note; ⌘D bookmarks the page; the Notes panel (⇧⌘N) lists them by chapter
- Export: Markdown, or Kindle’s My Clippings.txt format (works with Readwise, Obsidian Kindle plugins and Clippings.io)
- Look Up: select a word and press ⌃⌘D, or use the bar above the selection; uses the macOS dictionary, offline
- About the book: the description from the book’s metadata is shown at the top of the panel
- Typography: any installed font or original / sans / serif, size 80–200%, five weight levels, line / paragraph / letter spacing, margins, text width, one or two columns, justified or left; built-in Literata font; built-in presets Compact / Standard / Large / Low Vision / E-ink plus custom presets
- Themes: paper, sepia, e-ink, dark or follow the system
- Writing direction: books set for vertical writing (Japanese 縦書き) open vertically with the next page on the left; Settings › Layout › Writing Direction forces vertical or horizontal for any book; Japanese and Korean books use their own system fonts
- Interface languages: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, French, German, Spanish
- Not included by design: store, account, sync, library
- First launch: Leaf is not notarized by Apple; allow it once in System Settings › Privacy & Security › Open Anyway

## How it compares

- Readest: open-source (AGPL-3.0) and cross-platform, with a library, sync (optional paid cloud), highlights, notes and text-to-speech. It can read a file in place but adds every opened file to its library (title, path, cover) and keeps running after the window closes. About 67 MB download, macOS 12+. Checked 30 October 2026 (release 0.12.16 and a hands-on test).
- Apple Books: built into macOS and opens EPUB and PDF, but does not import MOBI or AZW3, and copies books into its library.
- Calibre: opens MOBI, AZW3 and EPUB and is centered on library management (about 350 MB download, macOS 14+, GPL-3.0); its viewer can also be launched on its own.
- Leaf: opens all of these formats like documents, with no library, in a 5 MB native app. It keeps your reading position, highlights, notes and bookmarks in its own folder and can export them as Markdown or Kindle clippings.
